source_title: South Africa relishing U19 Women's T20WC 2027 challenge | ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup, 2027 - ICC
source_excerpt:
South Africa U19 women’s head coach Dinesha Devnarain believes her team will be challenged to their limits at the ICC Under-19 Women's T20 World Cup 2027 .
The third edition of the tournament, which will be hosted in Bangladesh and Nepal, will be staged between 21 January and 06 February 2027.
South Africa, who hosted the first edition of the tournament in 2023 and finished runners-up in 2025, have been slotted in Group B alongside New Zealand, Samoa and Pakistan.
“It's an exciting group and one that will challenge us in different ways,” Devnarain said.
“We have recently played Pakistan, so there is some familiarity there, while New Zealand and Samoa bring their own challenges.
“We faced both at the previous World Cup, but this is a new tournament with new players, and we certainly won't be taking anyone lightly.”
South Africa will take cues from their previous appearance in the tournament a year ago when it was hosted in Malaysia.
"What 2025 showed us is that South African women's cricket belongs on the biggest stage. We have been there, we know it is possible, and that should inspire us,” Devnarain believes.
"The motivation is not simply to get back to a final. It is to take the lessons from that experience, continue raising our standards and give this group every opportunity to go one step further."
But it isn’t just the last edition of the tournament. The current group of players also have the advantage of having experienced the sub-continental conditions firsthand.
The junior Proteas side had toured Pakistan for a five-match T20I series, which they triumphed by a 3-2 margin.

“The Pakistan series was incredibly valuable for this group, and not simply because we won it 3–2.
“Playing in subcontinent conditions gave us valuable experience, but more importantly, it tested our decision-making, adaptability and ability to respond when things weren't going our way.
"For me, the biggest learning was that talent alone is not enough at the international level. You need game awareness, clarity and the ability to repeat your skills under pressure." Devnarain added.
As they gear up for the U19 T20 World Cup, the goal is to go one step further than they did in 2025.
“Our ambition is to win the World Cup. I don't think we need to shy away from saying that. While our immediate ambition is to lift that trophy, our responsibility goes beyond January 2027.
“We want to develop future match-winning Proteas and leave South African women's cricket stronger than we found it.”
